LM Studio's agentic workflow platform now allows users to run tasks on Kimi K3, a model from Moonshot AI with 2.8 trillion parameters and a 1 million context window. Here's what you need to know.

Kimi K3 is now available on LM Studio Bionic.

A few days ago, LM Studio announced Bionic, a new application aimed at users who want to run agentic tasks on open-source models.

Bionic is designed for coding, research, and more complex work involving creating or editing documents and files.

Users can run models locally, or leverage larger, cloud-based open-source models when tasks require more compute, since they offer longer context windows, stronger reasoning, and tool-calling capabilities that smaller local models currently cannot match.

Here is LM Studio's original announcement:

For cloud models, Bionic uses a US-based Zero Data Retention inference service. That means all requests are processed on US servers, and prompts, files, and model outputs are not stored after processing.

Previously, users relying on cloud open-source models had access to DeepSeek V4, Pro, GLM-5.2, Kimi K2.6, and Kimi-K2.7-Code. Today, the company added Kimi K3, allowing users to use what many consider the most powerful open-source model currently available.

Through Bionic, Kimi K3 is priced at $3 per million input tokens, $0.30 per million cached input tokens, and $15 per million output tokens.

This pricing stands in stark contrast to the previously available models, which charged between $0.95 and $1.74 for input tokens and between $3.48 and $4.50 for output tokens.

Still, the addition of Kimi K3 is a welcome development, especially for users who want to tackle more demanding tasks through LM Studio Bionic.

LM Studio Bionic is available for Mac and Windows, and you can learn more here.

Do you run local models on your Mac? Drop us a comment and let us know.
